data.claim: Folds read event data by .get, so an unknown key is ignored and an absent key leaves the new field empty
data.falsifier: an item.completed with changelog garbage or without it fails or changes fold
data.probe: pytest tests/test_export_changelog_data.py (old shape, garbage shape, round-trip)
data.question: Does an extra optional key on item.completed/bug.fixed break older folds?

evidence.note: D-export (4) followed; forward-compat key optional; README updated

chunk_findings.detail: The `or it.changelog` fallback makes the task-side field *sticky*: when a completion event carries no `changelog` key (or carries one that `changelog_of` rejects), the value from an earlier `item.completed` for the same item is kept instead of being reset to `{}`. The field's own comment two hunks up states the invariant `{}` when none was given, and the sibling handler for the same key on the bug side does the opposite — `_h_bug_fixed` (model.py:1561) assigns `changelog_of(...)` unconditionally, so an absent key resets the bug to `{}`. Concrete sequence: `item.completed {changelog:{Added,"x"}}` → `item.reopened` → `item.completed {}`. The fold leaves `it.changelog == {Added,"x"}`, so a changelog export attributes an `Added` line to a closure whose event never supplied one. The identical sequence on a bug (`bug.fixed {Fixed,"y"}` → reopen → `bug.fixed {}`) instead yields `bug.changelog == {}`, dropping the earlier `Fixed` line. Same spec, same key, two different fold results depending on task vs bug; one of the two sites is necessarily wrong, and the task-side `or it.changelog` is the one that contradicts the field doc it was added with. (If the intended semantics were "last non-empty wins", then the bug side needs the same `or`; either way the two lines cannot both be correct.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/model.py:1309 (`_h_item_completed`: `it.changelog = changelog_of(ev.data.get("changelog")) or it.changelog`)

chunk_findings.detail: The preceding lines complete `T1` (`res = _mcp(repo, "ddflow_complete", id="T1", ...)` → `_state(repo).items["T1"]` is done), and the negative call then reuses the *same* id: `bad = _mcp(repo, "ddflow_complete", id="T1", changelog="Zzz: x")`. Since `ddflow_complete` on an already-done task is a state error, the tool returns a non-zero exit and a JSON error body ("already done") without the changelog ever being parsed, so both `assert bad["_meta"]["exit"] != 0` and `assert json.loads(bad["content"][0]["text"])` are satisfied. A concrete way this hides a defect: delete the changelog validation from the MCP `ddflow_complete` path entirely — this test still passes. To actually test what the name claims, the bad call must target a second, ready task (e.g. add `T2` via `_task(repo, "T2")` + `pass_pipeline(repo, "T2")`), or the completion of `T1` must be moved before an assertion on the error text that names the changelog reason.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_changelog_data.py::test_mcp_complete_records_the_changelog

chunk_findings.detail:
The first `bug fixed B1 --changelog "Security: closed a hole"` succeeds, so `B1` is fixed; the second invocation then repeats on the same, now-fixed bug: `run_cli(repo, "bug", "fixed", "B1", ... "--changelog", "nope")` with `assert code != 0`. If the CLI rejects re-fixing an already-fixed bug (the state machine almost certainly does), the non-zero exit comes from the already-fixed guard rather than from the invalid `"nope"` changelog, and the assertion proves nothing about changelog rejection — removing changelog validation from the `bug fixed` path would keep this test green. Use a second bug (`bug.found B2` + a passing regression test) for the invalid-changelog case, or assert the specific error text mentions the changelog categories.

(For completeness: I also considered `"internal"` being accepted as a skip alias, the `category: ""` shape of skip records, and the `replay` wording in the round-trip test, but the decision/research context is not visible in this part and the assertions are consistent with the rest of the file, so I am not reporting those.)
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_changelog_data.py::test_bug_fixed_takes_the_changelog_too

chunk_findings.detail: Both public API functions gain the new `changelog` parameter *in the middle* of the signature, immediately before the existing trailing `agent` parameter (`model: str = "", changelog: str = "", agent: str = ""` in `complete`; `lesson_rule: str = "", changelog: str = "", agent: str = ""` in `bug_fixed`). Any existing caller that supplies the last argument positionally now binds that value to `changelog` instead of `agent`, and `agent` silently defaults to `""`. Concretely, an old-style positional call `lifecycle.complete(repo, item, sha, False, model, "alice")` previously attributed the completion to agent `alice`; after this change the 6th positional becomes `changelog="alice"`, which `parse_changelog` rejects (unknown category), so the function returns `O.failed("item.completed", ...)` and the completion never happens — and the agent attribution is lost. The same applies to `knowledge.bug_fixed(..., "carol")`. Appending `changelog` after `agent` (or making it keyword-only) avoids the silent rebinding; a search for positional call sites should accompany the change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle.py:1372 (and ddflow/api/knowledge.py:568, `bug_fixed`)

chunk_findings.detail: The `or it.changelog` fallback makes the item changelog *sticky*: an `item.completed` event that carries no `changelog` key (or a malformed one) leaves whatever value a previous `item.completed` folded into `it.changelog` instead of resetting it to `{}`. This contradicts the field's own documented contract on `Item.changelog` ("{} when none was given") and is inconsistent with the sibling `bug.fixed` path, which assigns unconditionally (`bug.changelog = changelog_of(ev.data.get("changelog"))`) and therefore does reset to `{}`. Concretely, feeding the fold the event sequence `item.completed{changelog:{"category":"Added","line":"x","skip":false}}` followed by `item.completed{}` (the second completion carries no `--changelog`) yields `item.changelog == {"category":"Added","line":"x","skip":false}` rather than `{}`, so a changelog derived from the folded state republishes the stale "Added: x" line for a completion that no longer claims it; there is also no way to clear the field via any later completion, unlike `completion_evidence`, which can be cleared with an explicit empty `evidence`. Dropping the `or it.changelog` (or treating a missing/empty key as an explicit unset) makes the item and bug paths agree and restores the documented "{} when none was given" invariant.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/model.py:1309 (`_h_item_completed`, `it.changelog = changelog_of(ev.data.get("changelog")) or it.changelog`)

chunk_findings.detail: The only MCP negative case is issued as `_mcp(repo, "ddflow_complete", id="T1", changelog="Zzz: x")` immediately *after* the same test completed `T1` successfully on the line above, and it also drops the `model="claude-opus-5"` argument that the successful call (and every CLI `complete` invocation in this file) needed. So `bad["_meta"]["exit"] != 0` is satisfied by the already-done/missing-argument rejection before `changelog` is ever parsed. Delete the changelog validation from the MCP surface entirely and this assertion still passes; the MCP half of the "CLI/MCP parity" acceptance is therefore not actually tested for rejection, only for the happy path (`res["_meta"]["exit"] == 0` plus the recorded category). Contrast this with the CLI negative test at `test_a_bad_changelog_is_refused_before_anything_is_recorded`, which deliberately uses a task that has not been completed yet and additionally asserts the error text names the categories — the MCP test has neither safeguard.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_changelog_data.py::test_mcp_complete_records_the_changelog

chunk_findings.detail: The refusal check `code, _o, err = run_cli(repo, "bug", "fixed", "B1", "--regression-test", ..., "--changelog", "nope"); assert code != 0` re-issues `bug fixed` on `B1` that was successfully fixed by the immediately preceding call in the same test, and unlike the CLI complete test it never inspects `err`. Any non-zero exit (e.g. "bug B1 is already fixed", or a rejected duplicate regression-test) satisfies the assertion, so `--changelog nope` being silently accepted by the bug-fixed path cannot be detected here. To actually exercise the parser, the bad changelog must be passed on the *first* `bug fixed` for a bug (or on a second, distinct bug).

chunk_findings.detail: `it.changelog = changelog_of(ev.data.get("changelog"))` now overwrites unconditionally, so any `item.completed` / `bug.fixed` event that does not carry the `changelog` key *clears* the changelog folded from an earlier event for the same id. This is exactly the "sticky field" pattern that the line directly above it (`it.completion_evidence = ev.data.get("evidence", it.completion_evidence)`) still uses, and it is the pattern this line used before (`... or it.changelog`); the diff makes the two fields that are written by the same event, on the same branch, behave inconsistently. Concrete demonstration: fold `[Event("item.completed","T1",{"kind":"task","changelog":{"category":"Added","line":"new API","skip":false}},lamport=1), Event("item.completed","T1",{"kind":"task","evidence":{...}},lamport=2)]` — the second event, which is what any producer that predates this feature (or any re-completion/sha-recording path that re-emits `item.completed` without the optional key) emits, leaves `completion_evidence` intact but returns `items["T1"].changelog == {}`. The record of what shipped is silently dropped from fold and replay, which is the exact data-loss class the comment above (\"Third instance of this class in this series\") says was already fixed twice. `test_a_later_completion_without_the_key_resets_the_item_field` asserts this lossy outcome, so the test does not protect against it — if the intent is that the key is optional and `complete` \"never requires it\", absence must mean \"unchanged\" (or the write must be gated on `"changelog" in ev.data`), not \"clear\".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/model.py:1309

chunk_findings.detail: The `or it.changelog` fallback was dropped, so the changelog field is now unconditionally overwritten by the value carried on the current closing event. When that event does not carry the key (i.e. `ev.data.get("changelog")` is `None` → `changelog_of(...)` → `{}`), a previously folded changelog is silently erased. Note the line immediately above does the opposite for the sibling field — `it.completion_evidence = ev.data.get("evidence", it.completion_evidence)` is written with a default precisely so that a closing event lacking that key does **not** clobber what an earlier closing event recorded (the comment describes this as the third instance of that class). The same situation therefore applies to `changelog`: with a log holding `Event("item.completed","T1",{"kind":"task","changelog":{"category":"Added","line":"x","skip":false}})` followed by `Event("item.completed","T1",{"kind":"task"})` — literally the two events in the new `test_a_later_completion_without_the_key_resets_the_item_field` — the fold now returns `items["T1"].changelog == {}` instead of the recorded entry, and the answer depends on which of the two events happens to be folded last rather than on which one actually carried the data. That makes the fold non-commutative for merged/replayed logs (an event from a writer that predates the field, or any completion reached without `--changelog`, wipes the entry) and contradicts the intent's own forward-compat requirement that keyless ("old") events fold unchanged. The new test asserts the lossy behavior, so it certifies the regression instead of catching it; the previous `... or it.changelog` (or `ev.data.get("changelog", it.changelog)`) is what keeps the field intact for keyless events.
